tafsir: "Wisdom" means understanding, knowledge and eloquence. God commanded him to thank Him; the benefit of gratitude returns to the grateful, and God is not harmed if all of creation is ungrateful (Ibn Kathir).
insight: The gratitude meant here includes thanking God for the ability to obey Him (al-Mukhtasar).
keywords: al-hikmah, wisdom: sound understanding that leads to right action.

tafsir: Luqman advised the person closest and dearest to him, so he gave him the best of his knowledge, beginning with worshipping God alone. Shirk is the greatest wrong (Ibn Kathir).
insight: Shirk is an injustice against one's own self, since it leads to lasting loss (al-Mukhtasar).
hadith: When 6:82 was revealed ("those who do not mix their faith with injustice"), the Companions were distressed, asking who among them does no wrong. The Prophet ﷺ said it does not mean that, and recited Luqman's words in 31:13: the injustice is shirk (Bukhari and Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, via Ibn Kathir).
keywords: ya'izuhu: counsel that encourages good and warns against evil (al-Mukhtasar).
ya bunayya, "O my dear son": the tender diminutive.

tafsir: Worshipping God and honouring parents are paired often in the Qur'an, as in 17:23 (Ibn Kathir).
"Weakness upon weakness": the hardship of pregnancy (Mujahid); exhaustion upon exhaustion (Qatadah) (Ibn Kathir).
The mother's sleepless care is recalled to remind the child of her kindness, as in 17:24 (Ibn Kathir).
insight: Weaning within two years matches 2:233. Read with 46:15 (thirty months for carrying and weaning), Ibn Abbas and other imams derived that the shortest pregnancy is six months (Ibn Kathir).
keywords: wahn, weakness: strain added to strain.

tafsir: If parents try hard to draw their child into their false religion, he must not accept it, yet he must keep treating them with respect in worldly life. "Those who turn to Me" are the believers (Ibn Kathir).
insight: No creature is obeyed in disobedience to the Creator; keep ties and good companionship with such parents (al-Mukhtasar).
context: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said verses were revealed about him. When he became Muslim, his mother swore not to speak to him, eat or drink until he left his faith, arguing that God commanded him to honour his parents. The verse enjoining kindness to parents, with the command not to obey them in shirk, was then revealed (Sahih Muslim 1748, quoting 29:8). Al-Wahidi reports that 31:14 and 46:15 were revealed in the same connection.
hadith: "There is no obedience in disobedience to God; obedience is only in what is right" (Bukhari 7257, Muslim 1840, narrated by Ali).
keywords: ma'rufan: with what is recognised as good and decent.

tafsir: Even a sin the size of a mustard seed, hidden inside solid rock or anywhere in the heavens and earth, will be brought forth on the Day and placed in the scales (21:47; 99:7-8). Latif: His knowledge reaches the most hidden things. Khabir: aware even of an ant's steps in the darkest night (Ibn Kathir).
insight: The verse covers good deeds as well as bad: both will be brought forth and repaid (al-Mukhtasar).
keywords: mithqal, weight: the smallest measurable amount.

tafsir: Offer prayer properly at its times; enjoin good and forbid evil as far as you are able. Luqman knew that whoever does this will meet harm from people, so he told his son to be patient; such patience is among the weightiest commands (Ibn Kathir).
insight: These instructions are matters God has made binding, not optional (al-Mukhtasar).

tafsir: Do not turn your face away from people when you speak with them, looking down on them; be gentle and meet them with a cheerful face. Do not walk boastfully; God does not love the self-admiring boaster (Ibn Kathir; compare 17:37).
hadith: "Do not belittle any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face" (Sahih Muslim 2626, from Abu Dharr).
keywords: tusa''ir, from sa'ar, a tilt of the neck: turning the cheek away in disdain.

tafsir: Walk moderately, neither slow and lazy nor excessively fast. Do not raise your voice unnecessarily; Mujahid and others said the ugliest voice is the donkey's, so needless loudness is blameworthy (Ibn Kathir).
insight: Moderate walking shows dignity; the voice should not be raised to the point of disturbing others (al-Mukhtasar).
keywords: iqsid, be moderate, from qasd: the balanced middle way.
